_meta.note: Captured off the wire: one real `opencode acp` 1.19.1 turn whose ONLY tool call is a Crew MCP directive tool. The MCP server rode the `session/new` `mcpServers` array as a stdio element named `kirocrew-core` exposing `monitor_start` (a scratch stdio server answering the way Crew's monitor_start does); the model was a local OpenAI-compatible stub on a loopback port, so no provider credential and no network were involved, with a throwaway HOME, driven to call that tool once and then answer `done`. The project's `permission` was allow, because this capture is about naming rather than gating. The whole turn, in order. What this fixture is evidence FOR: opencode names an MCP tool `<server>_<tool>` with ONE underscore and emits no `_meta.kiro` anywhere, so `title` is the only channel naming the tool; `rawInput` is `{}` on the `tool_call` and complete on the following `in_progress` update; and the tool's own result text, directive marker included, arrives verbatim in `content[].content.text` and again in `rawOutput.output`. The marker itself grants nothing -- the directive is claimed out of band from the call's own rawInput (`dashboard/directive_queue`), never from this text. Reduced at capture through scripts/capture_acp_compaction.py's own reduce_frames: the product's redact_text scrub, the scratch working directory replaced with <cwd> and the home directory with ~, the session id replaced with the synthetic opencode-session-1 and message ids with msg-N, the available_commands_update inventory dropped, and each configOptions select cut to its current option.
